### Rebuild with tools/regen_ef_currency_merge.py after any E&F or hotfix update.
###
### Source: E&F's own common/building_groups/00_ef_building_groups.txt,
### one field changed:
###   is_government_funded = yes  ->  is_government_funded = no
###
### THIS IS HALF OF THE OWNERSHIP CHANGE, not an optional extra, and
### leaving it out was a regression that cost a test round. building_bank
### with ownership_type = self gives the bank shares for a company to hold;
### this is what stops the treasury from paying for it. Without it the
### building panel reads "government" -- correctly, because the money still
### moves that way -- with a company named on the ownership tab that earns
### nothing from it. Suppress it with --government-funded-bank.
###
### And it is not a free switch. is_government_funded means the treasury pays
### the building's inputs and wages and takes its output. Off, the central
### bank is an ordinary private business, and on a 1836 British save it makes
### 200 bonds plus currency against about 2.5K of inputs and wages. As a
### government building that gap is state spending; as a private one it is
### profit, dividends and investment-pool inflow, every month, for whoever
### owns the central bank. That is the price of the ownership working at all.

REPLACE:bg_bank = {
	category = development

	always_possible = yes

	inheritable_construction = no
	is_government_funded = no

	economy_of_scale = no

	lens = government

	urbanization = 20
	infrastructure_usage_per_level = 0
	economic_contribution = 0 
}
